combo_label: The Pub × Silly English Things × Vikings

entries.clue: Village afternoon of bric-a-brac, cake stalls and a crackly tannoy
Stinging hedgerow plant; a Dorset inn crowns whoever eats the most
Named holder of a permit, whether for a bar, a taxi or a betting shop
Hallway dial tapped hopefully before anyone commits to a day out
Unfree labourer on a Norse farm, lowest of the social heap
Turf-walled Norse dwelling, one roof over family, hearth and beasts
What you give at the counter, the final one called before closing
Christmas show where the audience bellows 'he's behind you!'
Heavy pint pot with a grip on the side, and slang for the face
Give and ___: the second verb was a Norse import that ousted ours
Outlying hamlet in Norse; now the tail of many an English place name
Little marker jumped from hole to hole to keep the count at cards
Bell-jingling folk dance performed with hankies and sticks
Quarter of a pint in imperial measure, and what a fish breathes by
